editorial.marketOverview: Saturday US cash markets remain closed. The latest observed Friday session featured Nasdaq Composite -5.28%, Nasdaq 100 -5.6%, approximately -11% SOX, secondary QQQ -5.67% and reported VIX close 37.66. Semiconductors materially underperformed, while approximate breadth remained negative. These are Friday observations, not live Saturday prices.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the 13:25 EST snapshot, no independently confirmed material change in the expected November 23–25 path emerged. Reuters' November 20 SEC Nvidia accounting-investigation report remains incorporated, with no verified new SEC finding. November 21 reporting reprises this event. Financial Times reports Amazon is in advanced talks to buy AI startup Decart for roughly $7.5bn, but a transaction is not confirmed and the report does not establish a market response. Open Watch remains at 174 events, updated 2026-11-21T00:44:37+00:00.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Friday's much deeper SOX loss relative to QQQ/Nasdaq suggests leadership de-risking and raises the risk of continued pressure. Extreme VIX and oversold conditions also permit a sharp countertrend rally. The older 10Y 4.94% and 2Y 4.65% pair implies +29 basis points, not +2900, but it is historical and must not be presented as a current synchronized curve. Friday 10Y 4.93% cannot be paired with a different-time 2Y as live spread. VXN, FedWatch, directly synchronized breadth and matched Brent/WTI futures contracts are not verified. SEC scrutiny and AI financing concerns are risks, not proof of the causal allocation of Friday's decline.
editorial.threeDayPath: Monday November 23: assess QQQ/NVDA/SOX/SMH reaction to existing regulatory headlines and flash PMI; watch whether breadth and volatility confirm stabilization or continuation. Tuesday November 24: consumer confidence and ADI/Dell earnings test hardware demand and guidance. Wednesday November 25: scheduled GDP, PCE/personal income, durable goods and Beige Book can shift yield and Fed expectations. The baseline remains bearish elevated downside; an oversold rebound is plausible but not confirmed.
editorial.bullCase: A relief rally becomes credible only with synchronized QQQ/SOX/SMH strength, improving advance-decline breadth and a sustained decline in VIX/VXN. Better-than-feared PMIs and hardware guidance, together with easing yields and Fed pricing, could support recovery. None is yet an observed Monday response.
editorial.bearCase: Renewed NVDA and SOX underperformance, deteriorating breadth, stubbornly elevated volatility, hawkish rates repricing or weak hardware guidance would confirm continuation. A formal escalation of the accounting investigation would be a new catalyst if verified; no such escalation was established in this run.
editorial.watchNext: Verify Monday opening QQQ, SOX, SMH, NVDA, VIX and VXN on aligned timestamps; measure venue-specific breadth; retrieve paired Treasury 2Y/10Y from primary sources, CME FedWatch and maturity-matched Brent/WTI.
